title: There is a pharmacy
summary: Say what there is in a place with هُنَاكَ, ask 'is there…?' and find a pharmacy that is open late.
intro: هُنَاكَ means 'there', and at the start of a sentence it means 'there is' or 'there are': هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّة قَرِيبَة (there is a pharmacy nearby). To ask, put هَلْ in front: هَلْ هُنَاكَ بَنْك هُنَا؟ (is there a bank here?). Its partner هُنَا means 'here'. The noun after هُنَاكَ is usually indefinite: no الـ.
objectives: Say 'there is' and 'there are' with هُنَاكَ
Ask for medicine for a headache at a pharmacy

realLife.title: A late-night headache
realLife.story: After a long, hot day in the city, Daniel has a bad headache, and it is already ten o'clock at night. He goes down to Uncle Hassan, the doorman of his building, and asks if there is a pharmacy nearby. In Egypt many pharmacies stay open very late, and some never close at all.

sentences.en: There is a pharmacy near here.
sentences.literal: there (is) a pharmacy near from here

mistakes.why: After hunāka ('there is') the noun is normally indefinite: no al-.

sentences.ar: هَلْ هُنَاكَ بَنْك فِي هٰذَا الشَّارِع؟
sentences.en: Is there a bank on this street?
sentences.literal: (question) there (is) a bank in this street

sentences.en: There are many mosques in the city.

mistakes.why: ṣaydaliyya (pharmacy) is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too.

sentences.en: Do you have any medicine for a headache? (to a woman)
sentences.literal: (question) at you (is) medicine for the headache

dialogue.title: Is there a pharmacy near here?
dialogue.culture: In Egypt people call a pharmacist doctor (دُكْتُورَة for a woman), and they often ask the pharmacist for advice before they see a doctor. An older man such as a doorman is politely called عَمّ (uncle), even if he is not family.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر يَا عَمّ حَسَن! آسِف، الْوَقْت مُتَأَخِّر، لٰكِنْ عِنْدِي صُدَاع شَدِيد.
lines.en: Good evening, Uncle Hassan! Sorry, it is late, but I have a terrible headache.
segs: uncle (also a polite title for an older man)

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا ابْنِي! سَلَامَتُكَ. هَلْ تُرِيدُ دَوَاء؟
lines.en: Good evening, my son! Get well soon. Do you want some medicine?
segs: get well soon (lit. your safety, to a man)

lines.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. هَلْ هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّة قَرِيبَة مِنْ هُنَا؟
lines.en: Yes, please. Is there a pharmacy anywhere near here?

lines.ar: هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّات كَثِيرَة فِي الْحَيّ. الصَّيْدَلِيَّة الْأُولَى فِي آخِرِ الشَّارِع، لٰكِنَّهَا مُغْلَقَة الْآن.
lines.en: There are many pharmacies in the neighbourhood. The first one is at the end of the street, but it is closed now.

lines.ar: مُغْلَقَة؟ يَا خَسَارَة! وَهَلْ هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّة مَفْتُوحَة فِي اللَّيْل؟
lines.en: Closed? What a shame! And is there a pharmacy that is open at night?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! الصَّيْدَلِيَّة الثَّانِيَة بِجَانِبِ مَحَطَّةِ الْمِتْرُو، وَهِيَ مَفْتُوحَة لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا.
lines.en: Of course! The second pharmacy is next to the metro station, and it is open day and night.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا عَمّ حَسَن! أَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهَا الْآن مَشْيًا، فَالْمَحَطَّة قَرِيبَة.
lines.en: Thank you, Uncle Hassan! I will walk there now, because the station is close.
segs: uncle (also a polite title for an older man)

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَنَا الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
lines.en: Good evening! I am Dr Mona. How can I help you?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا دُكْتُورَة. عِنْدِي صُدَاع قَوِيّ مُنْذُ الْعَصْر. هَلْ هُنَاكَ دَوَاء جَيِّد؟
lines.en: Good evening, doctor. I have had a strong headache since the afternoon. Is there a good medicine for it?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هُنَاكَ حُبُوب مُمْتَازَة لِلصُّدَاع. خُذْ حَبَّة وَاحِدَة الْآن، وَحَبَّة بَعْدَ سِتِّ سَاعَات.
lines.en: Yes, there are excellent tablets for headaches. Take one tablet now, and another one after six hours.

lines.ar: حَبَّة الْآن، وَحَبَّة بَعْدَ سِتِّ سَاعَات. فَهِمْتُ. هَلْ هُنَاكَ نَصِيحَة أُخْرَى؟
lines.en: One tablet now, and one after six hours. I understand. Is there any other advice?

lines.ar: هَلْ كُنْتَ فِي الشَّمْس الْيَوْم؟ اِشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا، فَالْجَوّ حَارّ جِدًّا.
lines.en: Were you out in the sun today? Drink lots of water, because the weather is very hot.

lines.ar: نَعَم، كُنْتُ فِي الشَّارِع كُلَّ الْيَوْم. كَمْ ثَمَنُ الدَّوَاء، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
lines.en: Yes, I was out in the street all day. How much is the medicine, please?

lines.ar: عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا فَقَطْ. وَهٰذِهِ زُجَاجَةُ مَاء بَارِد، هَدِيَّة مِنَ الصَّيْدَلِيَّة!
lines.en: Only twenty pounds. And here is a bottle of cold water, a present from the pharmacy!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُورَة! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه أَنَّ هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّة مَفْتُوحَة فِي اللَّيْل.
lines.en: Thank you so much, doctor! Thank goodness there is a pharmacy open at night.

reading.title: Uncle Hassan's advice
reading.ar: هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّات كَثِيرَة فِي الْحَيّ. الصَّيْدَلِيَّة الْأُولَى مُغْلَقَة فِي اللَّيْل. الصَّيْدَلِيَّة الثَّانِيَة بِجَانِبِ مَحَطَّةِ الْمِتْرُو، وَهِيَ مَفْتُوحَة لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا. هُنَاكَ أَيْضًا بَنْك وَمَقْهَى، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ مُسْتَشْفَى قَرِيب.
reading.en: There are many pharmacies in the neighbourhood. The first pharmacy is closed at night. The second pharmacy is next to the metro station, and it is open day and night. There is also a bank and a café, but there is no hospital nearby.

quiz.prompt: How do you ask 'Is there a bank here?'
What is the opposite of مَفْتُوح?
Why can't Daniel go to the first pharmacy?
What does Dr Mona tell Daniel to do?
options: Take one tablet now and one after six hours

quiz.prompt: Which letter is not an emphatic consonant?

completion: Well done! You can say what there is in your neighbourhood, ask 'is there…?' and get help at a pharmacy.
